issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to use a modifiable List<Meal> for the 'orders' attribute, but the provided helper utilities and the reference solution use arrays (Meal[]) and ArrayHelpers for array manipulation. This mismatch (List vs array) creates a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which data structure to implement and which utilities to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification with the codebase: either (A) update the problem statement to require a Meal[] orders array (and mention using ArrayHelpers), or (B) change the template and solution to use a modifiable List<Meal> (and provide appropriate List helper methods). Ensure all examples and UML/text consistently refer to the same type.

issues.description: The problem statement contains a contradiction regarding the 'stock' attribute: one section describes it as a final instance field initialized in the constructor, while a later note explicitly requires the 'stock' attribute to be static (shared across instances). The reference solution implements stock as a static final field. This contradictory guidance can mislead students about whether to implement stock as an instance or a static attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement: state explicitly whether 'stock' is an instance final field or a static shared field. If the intended design is a shared stock, update the earlier description to say 'a static final Stock stock (shared across all instances)' so it matches the later note and the reference solution. If instead the stock should be per-instance, remove the requirement that it must be static and update the solution/template accordingly.
